summary:
Same-sex sexual activity is not criminalized. It has been legal since 1832. The age of consent is 14 under Criminal Code article 308bis, with a three-year close-in-age exemption.

Article 14(II) of the 2009 Constitution prohibits and punishes discrimination based on gender identity.

The Law Against Racism and All Forms of Discrimination defines discrimination to include gender identity and defines transphobia. It amended Penal Code article 281 to criminalize gender-identity-based discrimination. Dissemination and incitement to discrimination are punishable by one to five years imprisonment.

Since 2010, Penal Code article 40bis aggravates penalties for crimes motivated by grounds including gender identity.

The Gender Identity Law was passed by the Chamber of Deputies on 19 May 2016, by the Chamber of Senators on 20 May 2016, signed on 21 May 2016 and took effect on 1 August 2016. It permits persons over 18 to change name, sex and photograph on legal documents before the Civil Registry Service. The procedure is confidential and to be completed within 15 days. It requires a psychological test of voluntary assumption of identity. It does not require sex reassignment surgery. The change is reversible once only.

The first legal gender change under the law was completed on 1 August 2016 by activist Pamela Valenzuela.

The reassigned sex is not recognized for purposes of marriage. In November 2017 the Supreme Court invalidated as unconstitutional a June 2017 Supreme Electoral Tribunal instruction that had directed recognition. An appeal was filed to the Inter-American Court of Human Rights in May 2018. Article 63 of the Constitution limits marriage to heterosexual couples.

Same-sex couples may register free unions. The Civil Registry recognized such unions in December 2020. A Plurinational Constitutional Court ruling of 22 June 2022 obliging registration took effect on 20 March 2023. Regulations were modified by 21 July 2023 to provide the same requirements and timings as for heterosexual couples. Fifteen couples had registered by January 2023 under Inter-American Court Advisory Opinion OC-24/17, which had been issued in January 2018.

Legal protection is weakly enforced. The Ombudsman reported that 64 LGBT people were murdered in 2017. Only 14 cases were investigated. None resulted in a sentence.

Societal discrimination against LGBT people is reported as not uncommon. Bolivia's first virtual survey of LGBTI people, reported in December 2024, found extensive exclusion.

A 2017 ILGA poll found 64% agreed transgender people should have the same rights, 63% believed they should be protected from employment discrimination and 53% believed they should be allowed to change legal gender.
tangentialFactors:
The Gender Identity Law was adopted despite low voter support, with trans activists drawing on access to ruling-party legislators. Contradictory heteronormative laws were adopted alongside it. Both organised religion and LGBT activists were constituents of the ruling party.

Protection on grounds of sexual orientation parallels gender-identity protection. It is prohibited under the Constitution and criminalized under Penal Code article 281 as amended. Dissemination and incitement are punishable by one to five years imprisonment. Article 40bis aggravates penalties for orientation-motivated crimes since 2010.
localsOnly:
Transgender people may serve openly in the military under a 2013 Armed Forces announcement effective in 2015. Homosexuality in the military continues to be described as taboo, with discretion advised. A 2014 report documented anonymous testimony of discrimination and sanctions against gay soldiers.

Single people regardless of sexual orientation may adopt. Same-sex couples in a free union are permitted to adopt under Article 84 of the Child and Adolescent Code.

Men who have sex with men have been permitted to donate blood since 10 July 2019 under amended Supreme Decree 24547. A prior ban had classified homosexual and bisexual men as a high-risk group.
outOfScopeNotes:
Entry and visa rules for transgender visitors, including whether documents with changed markers are accepted, are not sourced in the inventory.

Screening procedures that could risk outing, bathroom and facilities rules, and access to gender-affirming care for visitors are not sourced in the inventory.

Whether the 2017 murder and investigation figures include identified transgender victims, and whether convictions occurred after 2017, is unresolved in the inventory.
